title: Add self-queued fix backlog line to athena status
summary: Add one line to `athena status` counting requests Athena queued for itself (steward channel, which Hestia requests also use) and how many have run, for the last 7 days and in total. The owner uses it to spot a stuck backlog.

defaults_applied.how: Unit tests and cargo test, clippy and fmt criteria
Criteria check the rendered counts, not that wiring exists
A zero-backlog case prints explicit zeros
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (StatusView, Athena::status at ~1187, scan_jobs, state_name, text rendering) and crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs (REQUEST_CHANNEL = "steward" at line 335, DRAINED_CHANNELS, open-request helper near line 373) and crates/athena-data/src/records.rs (Request has job, text, received_at, channel). The count is measured directly from Request.channel and received_at, and from each job's state.

Self-queued means a Request whose channel is REQUEST_CHANNEL ("steward"). I did not find a separate Hestia channel, so I assume Hestia requests use the same channel. The producer must confirm this in crates/athena-core/src/hestia*; if Hestia uses another channel, include it.

Has run means the job has left the queued state: it is running, or it reached a terminal outcome such as landed, rejected or closed. Queued-but-untouched jobs are the backlog. Terminal state is judged with the existing state_name and is_terminal helpers.
Last 7 days is measured by Request.received_at against the current time already used by status. Status stays read-only, and no new record type is added, so records validation needs no change.

Field meaning: Request.channel is a free string. Its documented use is routing the drain (steward.rs REQUEST_CHANNEL and DRAINED_CHANNELS), and it already marks steward-queued requests, so it is reused without change.
Goal and audience: the owner reads athena status to see whether self-queued fixes are piling up.
Standing defaults apply: tests pass, clippy is clean, and a CHANGELOG.md entry is added.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs builds records with steward-channel and cli-channel requests, some inside and some outside 7 days, some run and some still queued. The test asserts the rendered line shows the right counts for the last 7 days and in total, and that cli-channel requests are not counted. Verify by running `cargo test -p athena-core status`.

With no steward-queued requests, the line still prints with zeros (for example 0 queued, 0 run), so an empty backlog shows as an explicit count and is not hidden. A unit test covers this and is run with `cargo test -p athena-core status`.

The diff to crates/athena-core/src/status.rs adds a line to the `athena status` text output. It reads like `self-queued fixes  last 7d: N queued, M run · total: N queued, M run` and reports both the queued and run counts for both windows. It counts only requests whose channel is steward::REQUEST_CHANNEL, not a duplicated literal.

`cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass. Existing status tests and the xtask spec tests that check status labels still pass, with the Hestia spec_gaps label check updated if it applies.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry recording the new status line.

out_of_scope: Alerting or automatic action on a stuck backlog
Changing how the drain queues or runs steward requests
Adding new record types or fields
